title: Postoperative Fever Curve Workup
scenario: A 58-year-old client is on postoperative day 3 following a colon resection. The nurse reviews the temperature curve and associated findings recorded over the past 24 hours.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the temperature curve and accompanying findings, which conclusion best fits the trend?

options.text: A rising fever with escalating WBC and purulent wound drainage suggests a developing surgical site infection
The pattern reflects an expected inflammatory response that requires no follow-up
The findings are most consistent with atelectasis on postoperative day 1
The trend indicates a transfusion reaction from blood products

questions.rationale: A climbing fever paired with a rising WBC and new purulent drainage from a warm, reddened incision on postoperative day 3 is the classic timeline for a surgical site infection rather than a benign inflammatory response.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Given the worsening trend, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the surgeon about the fever curve and wound changes
Obtain a wound culture as ordered before starting antibiotics
Assess and document the incision and drainage characteristics
Monitor for signs of evolving sepsis
Reassure the client this is a normal healing fever and take no action
Apply a heating pad directly over the incision

questions.rationale: The rising fever curve with purulent drainage warrants provider notification, a culture before antibiotics, careful wound assessment, and vigilance for sepsis. Dismissing the fever or applying heat to a possibly infected wound is inappropriate.
